title: Growing Up With Nature
seo_title: Growing Up With Nature Class 4 EVS Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 4)

standard_text: How plants grow from seeds; what seeds need to sprout; how seeds are spread; young ones of animals; animals that lay eggs and those that give birth; life cycles of plants and animals; growing up (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 4).

key_big: Seeds need water, air and warmth to sprout.
key_sub: All living things grow and change.
body_html:
How to think about it

A seed sprouts when it gets water, air and warmth; first the root comes out, then the shoot. It grows into a seedling and then a plant with flowers, fruits and seeds. Seeds are spread by wind (cotton), water (coconut), animals (burrs that stick, fruits that are eaten) and by pods that burst.

Animals grow too. Some lay eggs (hens, frogs, snakes) and some give birth (cows, cats, humans). Their young have special names: a calf, a kitten, a chick, a tadpole. Frogs and butterflies change shape as they grow: this is metamorphosis.

Example

Young one of a sheep?

it says baa

Answer: a lamb

Example

How do cotton seeds spread?

light and fluffy

Answer: by the wind

Common mistakes

  • Thinking seeds need light to sprout.
  • Thinking all animals lay eggs.
  • Calling a tadpole a fish.

faq.q: What does a seed need to sprout?
faq.a: Water, air and warmth; light and soil are needed as the young plant grows.

faq.q: Why are seeds spread far from the parent plant?
faq.a: So that the young plants get enough space, light and water to grow.
